text: Given Polymarket markets with a 1c spread and mid price between 0.2 and 0.8 (to avoid binary extremes), when we simulate a limit order at the best bid for 1 contract and record whether it is filled within the next 4 ticks (using continuous Level 2 snapshots), then the observed fill rate should be >0% vs the 0% rate from prior 15-min snapshots, subject to queue position risk and the fact that the earlier proxy used only top-of-book.

Given Polymarket markets with mid-price > 0.10 and spread = 1c, when placing a limit order at the best bid during UTC 5h–10h, then the net profit per attempt should exceed 0.8c vs the baseline of -0.674c, subject to the 0c maker fee invariant and no queue position guarantee.

Given high-volume Polymarket binary events with median 1c spread and mid-prices between 0.1 and 0.9, when placing a maker bid at the touch price (bid side), then the round-trip fill rate should exceed 15% (vs current 9% baseline) during UTC 5h–9h windows, subject to the invariant that total fees remain below 1c per contract filled.
